USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: The US should escalate tariffs on China to maximum levels, targeting the full $505 billion in Chinese exports to the US. This is a once-in-a-generation opportunity to restructure the US-China trade relationship on American terms, as China's retaliatory capacity is structurally limited by the trade deficit asymmetry.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The US has overwhelming leverage in this dispute. The trade deficit of $375 billion means China imports only $130 billion of US goods, while the US imports $505 billion from China - giving the US a 4:1 advantage in tariff ammunition (RAND analysis). China cannot match US escalation tit-for-tat. The US economy is strong and can absorb short-term pain, while China faces greater structural exposure: exports to the US represent ~5% of China's economy versus only ~0.7% for US exports to China (RAND). China's currency has already depreciated 6% from 6.28 to 6.64 per dollar since April, signaling financial stress. The Trump administration sees this as a winning strategy for the 2018 midterms, and the political timing is optimal. Key US sectors at risk (agriculture, Boeing, autos) can be managed with targeted domestic support. The opportunity to force structural reforms on IP theft, forced technology transfer, and market access - and to weaken China's Made in China 2025 industrial policy - may not come again. Waiting risks China building alternative supply chains and reducing dependence on US markets.
key_factors: Trade deficit asymmetry: US imports $505B from China vs $130B exports, giving 4:1 tariff leverage
China's retaliatory capacity structurally limited - will run out of US goods to tariff
US economy strong enough to absorb short-term costs; China more export-dependent
Yuan depreciation of 6% (6.28 to 6.64) signals Chinese financial stress
Opportunity to force structural reforms on IP theft, tech transfer, Made in China 2025
Political timing favorable with 2018 midterm elections approaching
Targeted sectors (agriculture, autos, Boeing) manageable with domestic policy support
